intro.title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a function that evaluates mathematical expressions written in Reverse Polish Notation (RPN), a postfix notation where operators follow their operands. You will learn how to use a stack data structure to process the expression step-by-step, pushing numbers and applying operators to the top elements. The main technologies involved are JavaScript arrays (acting as the stack) and basic arithmetic operations. By the end, you will understand how RPN simplifies expression evaluation and be able to implement this classic algorithm in code.
intro.usecase: Reverse Polish Notation (RPN) is a fundamental algorithm used in scientific and financial calculators, where it enables efficient expression evaluation without parentheses. Developers encounter RPN when implementing formula parsers in spreadsheet applications like Excel or Google Sheets, where users can input complex mathematical expressions. It's also essential in compiler design for evaluating arithmetic expressions during code compilation, and in data processing pipelines that transform mathematical formulas. Understanding RPN helps you build robust calculation engines for financial dashboards, engineering tools, or any application requiring mathematical expression evaluation.
